packageRules.description: One pull request a week for everything that is not a major bump. Separate pull requests per dependency would arrive faster and be read less carefully; a weekly batch is small enough to review and rare enough not to become noise. Digest bumps ride along because a repinned action is the same action.

Pin GitHub Actions to a commit digest. A tag is mutable and points at whatever its owner last moved it to, which is the whole supply chain question for a workflow that runs with repository credentials. Renovate keeps the readable version in a trailing comment and bumps the digest on the weekly schedule above.

The Go toolchain gets its own pull request, never a group. It moves the compiler under every job at once, so when a build turns red on the week a toolchain bump lands, the pull request that changed it should be the one thing in it.
